key_insight: The paper synthesizes and adapts explainable AI (XAI) methods for protein language models, providing a practical taxonomy and guidance to interpret model outputs in biologically meaningful ways. It highlights which interpretability tools map best to sequence- and structure-level protein understanding and where gaps remain.
problem_solved: Addresses the black-box nature of protein language models by collating, evaluating, and contextualizing XAI techniques so practitioners can choose appropriate methods to derive biologically relevant explanations.
method: Systematic review and taxonomy of XAI methods applicable to protein LMs (e.g., attention analysis, feature attribution, probing, and representation disentanglement).
Mapping of techniques to interpretability goals (sequence motifs, structural contacts, functional sites) and discussion of evaluation criteria and biological validation strategies.
Identification of limitations and proposal of best practices and future research directions for benchmarking and combining XAI tools in protein modeling.
impact: Equips AI/ML and computational biology practitioners with a clear framework to interpret protein LM behavior, improve trust, and accelerate hypothesis generation and experimental validation. Standardized guidance reduces misuse of interpretability methods and helps prioritize biologically meaningful investigations.
visual_elements: Taxonomy flowchart linking XAI methods (attention, attribution, probes, disentanglement) to interpretability goals (motifs, structure, function).
Sequence-to-structure diagram showing example explanations: highlighted residues from attribution overlaid on 3D structure.
Comparison matrix (heatmap/table) of methods vs. criteria: granularity, biological relevance, required supervision, and computational cost.
Checklist infographic of best-practice steps for applying and validating XAI on protein LMs (preprocessing, method selection, biological validation, reproducibility).
paper_title: Towards the explainability of protein language models
